name.text: Reading percentiles from a cumulative frequency curve

questiontext.text:
The graph shows the cumulative frequency curve of the time, \(t\) minutes, that \({@n@}\) customers spent in a bank in Kisumu.

[[jsxgraph width="560px" height="400px"]] (function() { var jx = {#jx#}; var jy = {#jy#}; var x0 = {#xmin#}; var x1 = {#xmax#}; var n = {#n#}; var dy = {#dy#}; var sx = x1 - x0; var b = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard(divid, { boundingbox: [x0 - 0.09*sx, 1.12*n, x1 + 0.03*sx, -0.13*n], axis: false, grid: false, pan: {enabled: false}, zoom: {enabled: false}, showNavigation: false, showCopyright: false }); // small squares: 1 minute across, dy customers up; thicker lines every 10 minutes and every 5*dy var gx, iy; for (gx = x0; gx <= x1; gx += 1) { b.create('segment', [[gx, 0], [gx, n]], {strokeColor: ((gx - x0) % 10 === 0) ? '#a8a8a8' : '#e2e2e2', strokeWidth: ((gx - x0) % 10 === 0) ? 1 : 0.5, fixed: true, highlight: false}); } for (iy = 0; iy <= 20; iy += 1) { b.create('segment', [[x0, iy*dy], [x1, iy*dy]], {strokeColor: (iy % 5 === 0) ? '#a8a8a8' : '#e2e2e2', strokeWidth: (iy % 5 === 0) ? 1 : 0.5, fixed: true, highlight: false}); } b.create('segment', [[x0, 0], [x1, 0]], {strokeColor: '#000000', strokeWidth: 1.5, fixed: true, highlight: false}); b.create('segment', [[x0, 0], [x0, n]], {strokeColor: '#000000', strokeWidth: 1.5, fixed: true, highlight: false}); for (gx = x0; gx <= x1; gx += 10) { b.create('text', [gx, -0.04*n, String(gx)], {anchorX: 'middle', anchorY: 'middle', fixed: true, highlight: false, fontSize: 12}); } for (iy = 0; iy <= 20; iy += 5) { b.create('text', [x0 - 0.012*sx, iy*dy, String(iy*dy)], {anchorX: 'right', anchorY: 'middle', fixed: true, highlight: false, fontSize: 12}); } b.create('text', [x0 + sx/2, -0.1*n, 'Time (minutes)'], {anchorX: 'middle', anchorY: 'middle', fixed: true, highlight: false, fontSize: 13}); b.create('text', [x0 + 0.01*sx, 1.07*n, 'Cumulative frequency'], {anchorX: 'left', anchorY: 'middle', fixed: true, highlight: false, fontSize: 13}); var pts = []; for (var i = 0; i < jx.length; i++) { pts.push(b.create('point', [jx[i], jy[i]], {name: '', size: 2, face: 'o', strokeColor: '#1f4e9c', fillColor: '#1f4e9c', fixed: true, highlight: false, showInfobox: false})); } b.create('polygonalchain', pts, {borders: {strokeColor: '#1f4e9c', strokeWidth: 2, highlight: false}, fixed: true}); })(); [[/jsxgraph]]

Use the graph.

(a) Estimate the percentile \(P_{ {@k@} }\), to the nearest minute.

\(P_{ {@k@} } =\) [[input:ans1]] minutes [[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prt1]]

(b) Estimate how many customers spent more than \({@v@}\) minutes in the bank.

[[input:ans2]] customers [[validation:ans2]] [[feedback:prt2]]

generalfeedback.text:
(a) \(P_{ {@k@} }\) has \({@k@}\%\) of the customers below it. \({@k@}\%\) of \({@n@}\) is \({@pk@}\), so go across from \({@pk@}\) on the cumulative frequency axis to the curve, then down: \(P_{ {@k@} } \approx {@Pd@}\) minutes.

(b) Go up from \({@v@}\) minutes on the time axis to the curve, then across: about \({@belowd@}\) customers spent less than \({@v@}\) minutes. The cumulative frequency at a time counts every customer below that time, so the rest spent more: \({@n@} - {@belowd@} = {@cntd@}\), about \({@floor(cnt+1/2)@}\) customers. Answers within one small square on the cumulative frequency axis (\({@dy@}\) customers) are accepted.

questiondescription.text:
Statistics II: reading percentiles and counts from a cumulative frequency curve

Grade 12 CBE Core 3.1: Read a percentile from a cumulative frequency curve and estimate how many values lie above a given value.

Core

This question is original to this project and does not come from Cassell, D., Instone, S., Ling, J., Scruton, P. and Shilton, S., SMP AS/A2 Mathematics: Statistics 1 for Edexcel, Cambridge University Press, 2004.

INNODEMS CBC Grade 12 Mathematics, first draft by Ben Davies, 2026. Aligned to the KICD Senior School Curriculum Design, Core Mathematics Grade 12 (draft).

feedbackvariables.text: inr: is(ans1>a) and is(ans1<a+60); cfa: if inr then dispdp(float(cfat(ans1)),1) else 0;

truefeedback.text: You read across from \({@k@}\). \(P_{ {@k@} }\) has \({@k@}\%\) of the \({@n@}\) customers below it: go across from \({@pk@}\).
That is a number of customers, not a time. Read down to the time axis.

falsefeedback.text:
[[if test="inr"]]

At \({@ans1@}\) minutes the curve is at a cumulative frequency of about \({@cfa@}\). \(P_{ {@k@} }\) has \({@k@}\%\) of the \({@n@}\) customers below it.

[[else]]

Find \({@k@}\%\) of \({@n@}\), go across from it to the curve, then down to the time axis.

[[/if]]

truefeedback.text: That is how many spent less than \({@v@}\) minutes. The question asks about the other customers.

falsefeedback.text: Go up from \({@v@}\) on the time axis to the curve and across: that is how many spent less than \({@v@}\) minutes. The rest spent more.

qtest.description: Correct, to the nearest whole number
Count read within one small square
